walls.note: Bruges: the second enceinte of 1297 (double moat, earthen rampart, stone gates), converted into a bastioned fortress from 1614; traced from the Ferraris map (1777) along the main rampart.

landmarks.y1650: Cloth hall with the belfry on the Markt; the octagonal top dates from 1482-86 and carried a wooden spire until the fire of 1741, so in 1650 the tower was taller than today's 83 m (spire height not verified).
Gothic town hall on the Burg, 1376-1420.
The cathedral of Bruges (bishopric 1559) stood on the Burg opposite the town hall; demolished from 1799. Position approximate.
Double chapel on the Burg holding the relic of the Holy Blood (procession since the 13th c.).
Church with the brick tower of about 115 m; Michelangelo's Madonna (1504) inside.
Collegiate church of Sint-Salvator (cathedral only from 1834).
Princely beguinage of 1245 by the Minnewater; church rebuilt 1605.
Town palace of the lords of Gruuthuse.
